_comment: Everything Slate needs that is not source code. setup.bat reads this file,
downloads what is missing and puts it where the application looks for it.
None of it is committed: these are third-party builds with their own
licences, and between them they are the better part of a gigabyte. Pinning
them here rather than vendoring them keeps the repository a few megabytes
and makes an upgrade a one-line edit.
Set 'required' to false for anything the studio can work without - setup
reports those as skipped rather than failing the whole install.

components.name: python
components.title: Python 3.10 (portable)
components.why: Slate runs on it. Nothing is installed system-wide and no existing Python on the machine is touched.

components.name: pip
components.title: pip
components.why: Installs Slate's Python dependencies into the portable runtime.

components.name: ffmpeg
components.title: FFmpeg
components.why: Thumbnails, proxies and playback. The review and stock browser tabs need it.

components.name: postgresql
components.title: PostgreSQL 16 (binaries only)
components.why: The studio database. Only needed on the machine that runs Slate Central Server - a workstation that connects to an existing server can skip it.

components.name: olive
components.title: Olive video editor
components.why: Embedded in the review tab for cutting. Slate falls back to its own player when this is absent.

resolve._comment: Olive's nightly asset carries the build's commit hash in its filename, so a pinned link rots within the week. The release is looked up at setup time instead.

components.name: openrv
components.title: OpenRV
components.why: Used for review playback when it is present. There is no public Windows build, so this one is built or supplied by the studio - drop it in the folder below and Slate finds it.
